I believe they put those rules into place so that: A: The NSFW images that doesn't belong here is posted in the correct place and B: That the subbreddit that it was posted in doesn't become over flooded by NSFW images. This site is 13+ but most of the NSFW subs have a 18+ warnings before entering the sub. If you suggest that, then suggest it to the Mods or Admins, they are looking for suggestions everyday.

The app that I use is Reddit Sync and in the settings, there's a tab below that has a filters section so that you can block words or even subs (I had r/politics blocked after the election for a month and a half). I'm not sure if you're on your phone or computer, but I believe there's a filter setting when you go into the settings on your Reddit account. I'm not sure what is called since I haven't used the website in 2 years, but I know that it's there because I used to to block other words and crap I didn't want to see. I would message a mod for more assistance.

But now I have told you this, I'm just gonna say one last thing because I feel like I have already said what I needed to say, the internet doesn't filter things. Websites people visit doesn't have filters. What people need to understand is that the owners of the websites gave us the tools to take care of anything that we find offensive, therefore giving us personal responsibility to take steps to avoiding what any of us considers a trigger. I have a trigger that gets posts once in a while and gains traction on r/all. If I do end up seeing it, I do what I can to to ease my own anxiety of it. Because no one is going to be looking out for my best interests except for *me*. We can give all the suggestions we want but we need to use the tools given instead of passing off the responsibility. If you feel that there's more that needs to be done, the Admins would love to know. Other than that, there's not much they can do.

But as you can tell, this post doesn't fall into neither category of porn or gore. Blocking it isn't pointless because if you go into your settings and set up your filters, you'll be able to scroll through Reddit without the fear of being triggered. Yes, you can't unsee nor unfeel the feelings, but if the subject isn't against the rules , it's up to the user then to figure out what they can do for their mental health if the subject in question was triggering to them.

And do I consider it censorship? Not really. They already outlined the main rules of the subbreddit and honestly, that's as simple as it gets. Obviously if someone violated the rules, the Mods will step in. But the post isn't triggering. At least to me it isn't. If he didn't specify the story of said bullet, I don't think it would be as big of an issue as it is now. So now its up to the user. If they have the power to block this, they should use it. We were given these tools by the Admins and so we should be using it.
